## Complete `ofch` census

There are 43 reader-exact occurrences of 25 complete surfaces containing the
formal EVA sequence `ofch`, on 36 pages and 41 loci. The sequence is only a
selector: it is not assigned a sound, Latin expansion or free meaning.

| cohort | raw occurrences/forms | exact occurrences/forms | position |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| strict `ofch*` prefix | 30 / 15 | 25 / 13 | 21 medial, 4 final, 0 first |
| other complete wholes containing `ofch` | 28 / 17 | 18 / 12 | 15 medial, 2 final, 1 first |
| total | 58 / 32 | 43 / 25 | 36 medial, 6 final, 1 first |

Thirty-four of 43 occur on paragraph-start lines, but only one is itself the
paragraph opener; none is on a paragraph-end line. In the strict prefix set,
all 21 exact left edges and all 17 exact right edges are unique. This is good
geometry for an early content field, not for a repeated command formula, and
it also means that no recurring immediate phrase identifies the substance.

## Four `chor`-like complete words

The exact census contains 191 occurrences on 99 pages and 183 loci.

| complete whole | exact | key geometry | selected role | bold default |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `chor` | 176 | 161 medial; 0 true paragraph openers | content/plant-part head | **Blütenstand** |
| `pchor` | 10 | 7 first; 6 true paragraph openers | recipe/entry opening | **nimm** at true openings |
| `schor` | 3 | 2 first; third follows H2 and takes a value | item/subentry head | **Blütenstandsposten** |
| `lchor` | 2 | both Biology; no stable right neighbor | internal preparation field | **Blütenzubereitung** |

`pchor` and `chor` differ strongly: line-first placement is 7/10 versus 10/176
(two-sided Fisher p = 1.4721e-6), while true paragraph opening is 6/10 versus
0/176 (p = 3.9614e-9). The three medial `pchor` occurrences are dispatched as
recipe/entry markers rather than automatically spoken as an imperative.

`chor` has 41 reader-exact immediate contacts at 38 loci: 19 value contacts and
22 state contacts, including fifteen with `chol`. This supports a nominal
content carrier and the reproductive-plant-part lead. It still leaves
flower-head, seed-head and a broader plant part as rivals.

root_qualifications: The ofch/chor design predicts the already reported positional contrast. A shared noun can serve in different syntactic or record roles, and different complete forms can share a nominal class. Role-position separation alone does not distinguish a free semantic substring from learned wholes. No held protocol is specified in the actual draft despite the peer description.

GDT808 axis-specific structural transfer and semantic operator identity are different questions. A common semantic operation can have different observable distributional signatures under different carriers. A cross-axis classifier failure does not by itself falsify shared meaning.

The old report quote says169physicalfolios; GDT858 corrects these to169faces/90leaves. GDT865 independently supports only the whole-leaf primary nuisance thresholds, not all old cross-axis/null verdicts. This source correction remains authoritative; no replay started.

GDT560 and GDT459 restatements supply no changed contrast. IN was a source-overlap screen, not an empirical rejection of the general nomenclator mechanism; the IR peer wording explicitly rejected is narrowed accordingly.
limits: Preserve all four draft files and source comparisons. No exact identity decision on every possible family variant, no new experiment, no semantic result.
